toxic.introQuote: "Is my relationship toxic... or am I overreacting?"
toxic.introDesc: If this question keeps coming back, it's never by chance. A toxic relationship is not defined by arguments, but by repeated dynamics that generate fear, guilt, loss of self-esteem, or emotional confusion.
toxic.disclaimer: This test is neither a medical diagnosis nor a judgment.
toxic.disclaimerDesc: It's a lucid self-assessment tool to understand what you're really experiencing.
toxic.testInfo: 25 questions • About 5 minutes • Anonymous and free
toxic.reminderText: This test is purely indicative. It is by no means an exact and precise result, and should not be used to replace professional advice. If you believe your relationship is truly toxic or even dangerous, contact real specialists.

pervers.introQuote: “Am I living with a narcissist… or am I overreacting?”
pervers.introDesc: If this question keeps coming back, it is never by chance. Narcissistic abuse is not recognised by a single argument, but by repeated patterns that install doubt, guilt and a loss of self-esteem.
pervers.disclaimer: This test is neither a diagnosis nor a judgement.
pervers.disclaimerDesc: It is a caring reflection tool to help you put words on what you are really going through.

result.lowDesc: Your answers often differ, and that is not a problem: this test compares your tastes, not how solid your relationship is. Above all, you have plenty left to discover about each other.
result.mediumDesc: You share a good part of your tastes, with just enough differences to keep surprising each other. A very healthy balance.
result.highDesc: Your tastes are remarkably alike. Keep in mind that this percentage measures identical answers, not the strength of your love, which no score can capture.
result.lowAdvice: Take the time to talk through every topic that surprised you.

compat.t1d: Your answers diverge on several fundamentals: plans, pace of life, vision of the future. This is not a verdict on your relationship, it is a map of the topics worth putting on the table. Plenty of solid couples live very well with different visions, as long as they talk about them.
compat.t2d: You meet on a good part of the essentials and diverge on the rest. Spot the questions where your answers did not match: those are exactly the conversations that move a relationship forward.
compat.t3d: You are aligned on the essentials, with a few differences that enrich you rather than set you against each other. This is the most common profile among couples that last.
compat.t4d: Your fundamentals answer each other almost everywhere: values, plans, pace of life. A rare and precious base. Keep in mind that this percentage measures aligned answers, not the strength of your love.

divorce.disclaimer: This test is a personal reflection tool. It does not replace professional advice in any way.

bands.title: A relationship to protect
bands.desc: Several foundations (communication, trust, shared plans) need attention. Nothing is lost: these are exactly the topics to open up about together, without judging each other.

bands.title: A good base to build on
bands.desc: Your relationship rests on real foundations, with a few areas to work on. Spot the questions where your answers differ, those are your next projects as a couple.

bands.title: A solid relationship
bands.desc: You've built a stable, balanced relationship. Keep nurturing what works and talking about what stalls before it settles in.

bands.title: A very solid relationship

quiDeNous.setupDesc: You each vote in secret, then both answers are revealed at once. Time to find out whether you see things the same way…
quiDeNous.passeDesc: No peeking: the vote stays hidden until the reveal.
quiDeNous.accordTexte: You both picked the same person. One more point on the board.
quiDeNous.clashTexte: You don't see this one the same way at all. Talk it out, it's worth it!
quiDeNous.palier1Titre: You really don't see things the same way
quiDeNous.palier1Texte: Each of you has a version, and they barely overlap. That's not a problem at all: it mostly means you have things to tell each other. Go back over the rounds where you disagreed, that's where the best conversations are hiding.
quiDeNous.palier2Titre: One picture out of two in common
quiDeNous.palier2Texte: Half the questions you nail, the other half you miss completely. It's the most common score, and honestly the most interesting one: you know each other, but there are still blind spots. Worth digging into.
quiDeNous.palier3Texte: You see your relationship in roughly the same way, and it shows. The few disagreements left are usually about small everyday things… or about who sings the most out of tune.
quiDeNous.palier4Titre: You think alike, almost suspiciously so
quiDeNous.palier4Texte: You picked the same person on nearly every question. Either you know each other inside out, or one of you peeked over the other's shoulder. We'll let you argue about that one!
